pages.name: Same pieces
pages.text: 1/4 and 2/4 are both quarters. Put them together and you have 3 quarters, so 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4. The tops add, and the bottom stays, because it names the piece.

pages.name: Eighths and eighths
pages.why: The pieces are all eighths, so count them. 3 and 2 make 5, and the bottom stays 8.

pages.name: Different pieces
pages.text: Cut the half into quarters, and both have the same bottom, called a [[common denominator]]. Adding tops and bottoms instead gives 2/6, less than the half alone.

pages.name: Halves and eighths
pages.why: A half is 4 eighths, so 1/2 + 3/8 = 4/8 + 3/8. That makes 7 eighths, 7/8.

pages.name: Taking away
pages.text: Taking away works the same way. Cut the half into quarters, so 3/4 − 1/2 = 3/4 − 2/4. Take 2 quarters from 3, and 1/4 is left.

pages.name: Take a quarter
pages.why: A quarter is 2 eighths, so 5/8 − 1/4 = 5/8 − 2/8. Take 2 eighths from 5, and 3/8 is left.

pages.name: Past a whole
pages.text: On a timesheet, half an hour is 2 quarter-hours. Add 3/4 h and that makes 5 quarter-hours, 5/4 h. Four make a whole hour, so it's 1 1/4 h.

pages.alt: Bars for 1/2 add 3/4, each bar one hour, both now cut into pieces of size 1/4. Their shaded pieces have joined in the bottom bar, which shows 1 and 1/4.

pages.name: Two jobs
pages.task: Colour two jobs of 3/4 h on the hour bars. How long is that, as a mixed number?
pages.why: Six quarter-hours make one hour and 2 quarters more. 2/4 is a half, so it's 1 1/2 h.

pages.name: Two cables
pages.task: Two lengths of cable, 2 3/4 m and 1 1/2 m, are laid end to end. How long are they together?
pages.why: 3/4 + 1/2 is 5/4, which is 1 1/4. With the 3 whole metres, that makes 4 1/4 m.

pages.name: Break a whole
pages.text: There is only 1/4, not enough to take 3/4 from. Break the whole into 4 quarters, so 1 1/4 is 5/4. Take 3 quarters, and 2/4 is left.

pages.alt: A whole bar above a bar of 4 quarters with 1 shaded, together 1 and 1/4, and 1 and 1/4 − 3/4 written under them. The whole is cut into 4 quarters, and 5 quarters are counted, so the sum now reads 5/4 − 3/4. The last 3 quarters are taken away, leaving dashed outlines marked taken, and 2 quarters are left, so 5/4 − 3/4 = 2/4.

pages.name: Cut a length off
pages.task: A 3 1/4 m length of cable has 1 3/4 m cut off. How much is left?
pages.why: 1/4 isn't enough to take 3/4 from, so break one metre into quarters. Then 3 1/4 m is 2 5/4 m, and taking 1 3/4 m leaves 1 2/4 m, or 1 1/2 m.

pages.name: Halves and thirds
pages.task: Sixths are a common denominator for halves and thirds. What is 1/2 + 1/3?
pages.why: A half is 3/6 and a third is 2/6. Together they make 5/6.
